#Writing documentation

Every page of the documentation site is a Markdown file under docs/. The generator src/tools/docsite turns them into the static site under site/docs/. There is no framework and nothing is fetched at runtime; the pages render in Wren itself.

#The workflow

  1. Write or edit a .md file under docs/.
  2. If the page is new, add it to docs/_nav.txt so it appears in the sidebar where you want it. A page you forget is still generated and linked (it lands in a "More" section), so nothing is lost, but the order and the section are up to you.
  3. Run tools\docs_site.ps1. It regenerates site/docs/ and checks that every internal link and anchor resolves.
  4. Commit the .md and the regenerated site/docs/. The generation is deterministic (same input, same bytes), and CI fails if site/docs/ is out of date — the same rule as tools\changelog.ps1 -Check.

#The sidebar: docs/_nav.txt

The file lists the sections and the pages in each, in the order they appear. Its own header documents the format. In short:

Section Title
  page.md            a page whose label is its first heading
  page.md  Label     a page with an explicit sidebar label
  dir/*    Label      every .md of a directory, as a sub-group (an _index.md or README.md leads it)

#The Markdown it understands

The generator implements the slice of CommonMark and GitHub-flavored Markdown the docs use:

  • Headings # to ######. The first # heading is the page title. Each heading gets a stable #anchor.
  • Paragraphs, bold (**x**), italic (*x* or _x_), inline code, and hard breaks (two trailing spaces).
  • Lists, bullet (-, *, +) and ordered (1.), nested by indentation.
  • Links [text](url). A relative link to another doc — remote.md, api/dom.md, ../README.md — is rewritten to the site's URL automatically. A link that leaves docs/ becomes a GitHub link. Keep writing links as .md paths; do not hand-write .html.
  • Images ![alt](src). Put image files under docs/ and reference them relatively.
  • Blockquotes > and thematic breaks (---).
  • Tables, GitHub style, with :---: alignment.

  • Fenced code blocks with a language for syntax highlighting:

    Odin
        main :: proc() { }

    The highlighter knows odin, c, js / javascript, powershell, json, rust and widl. Colouring happens at generation time; there is no client-side highlighter.

A bare <!-- comment --> and a few inline tags (<sub>, <a>, …) pass through. Anything the generator does not understand is shown as escaped text rather than failing, so a mistake is visible on the page.

You rarely need these; they belong to docs/conformance.md.

#Rules of thumb

  • One # heading per page, at the top. The site, the search index and the breadcrumbs use it as the title.
  • Link to other docs by their .md path. Never write a site .html URL by hand.
  • Keep headings in order (don't jump from # to ###): the table of contents and screen readers follow the levels.
  • The site has a dark and a light theme (it follows the operating system). Do not assume a background colour in any inline HTML you add.
